description: Synthetic, grouped AI infrastructure incidents for E07 QLoRA training. The frozen E05 quality set is test-only and is not copied here.

train: A single-GPU adapter job loads successfully but fails in backward after the micro batch is raised from one to six; the allocator reports CUDA out of memory.
The first optimizer step cannot reserve another activation tensor on the GPU, while the model snapshot and local disk remain healthy.
Increasing sequence length makes a QLoRA run fail during gradient computation with only a few MiB free on the device.
Fine-tuning completes with checkpointing enabled but exhausts device memory when checkpointing is disabled under the same data and driver.
A training worker reaches the GPU allocation limit during backward; no inference process or unrelated CUDA application is running.
validation: The adapter trainer initializes, then the CUDA allocator fails only after per-device batch size is increased; reducing it previously completed.
Backward on a long training example requests more device memory than remains, although package import and model loading both succeeded.

train: The online engine has no free KV blocks when eight long prompts decode together, but short low-concurrency requests still complete.
Serving starts normally and then preempts 8K sequences repeatedly because every paged-attention cache block is occupied.
Four long requests fit, while admitting twelve with the same model stalls allocation despite stable model-weight memory.
Context growth from 2K to 8K consumes the remaining GPU KV capacity and new requests wait for blocks rather than failing model load.
The scheduler reports zero available KV cache blocks at peak concurrency; lowering active sequence count restores service.
validation: Near-maximum prompts fill the token cache and trigger recomputation, while the CUDA allocator does not report a weight-loading OOM.
The model remains resident, but long-context traffic cannot admit another sequence because its KV block pool is exhausted.

train: The host sees the NVIDIA device, but the installed PyTorch CUDA runtime requires a newer driver and CUDA initialization fails.
A custom CUDA operator was built for another CUDA major version and cannot resolve symbols against the active torch wheel.
nvidia-smi works in WSL2 while torch reports that the host driver is incompatible with the bundled CUDA runtime.
After upgrading the CUDA-enabled torch build, kernel loading fails before any model file is opened because the driver branch is too old.
The extension loader reports an ABI mismatch between the active CUDA runtime and the version used to compile its shared object.
validation: GPU discovery succeeds outside Python, yet torch cannot initialize because its wheel targets a CUDA release unsupported by the current driver.
A compiled attention kernel fails with undefined CUDA symbols immediately after torch was replaced with a wheel from another runtime family.

train: The benchmark CLI imports an old datasets package that calls an API removed by the newly upgraded PyArrow package.
Installing an unrelated tool changed pydantic and transformers to releases outside the serving stack's supported ranges.
The environment resolver reports incompatible tokenizers requirements and vLLM now fails during Python import before touching CUDA.
Packages from two experiments share one virtual environment and require mutually exclusive versions of a common dependency.
A partial pip upgrade leaves benchmark extras and the core inference package on inconsistent releases, producing an import AttributeError.
validation: The application starts in a clean lockfile environment but crashes in the current environment after transitive libraries were upgraded independently.
Importing the serving CLI fails because installed library versions violate its declared dependency constraints; hardware checks have not started.

train: The node cannot reach the model registry over HTTPS and has no cached configuration or weight files for the pinned revision.
Every repository metadata request is reset by the network, while a verified model snapshot can be transferred from another machine.
An offline inference host starts with an empty model cache and fails before config.json can be resolved from the remote repository.
Corporate egress blocks the model hub although package mirrors and local applications remain reachable; the required weights are absent.
The serving process retries remote HEAD requests and reports network unreachable because no local snapshot exists for the requested revision.
validation: Model startup times out downloading tokenizer and weight artifacts, but a domestic mirror is reachable and the intended commit is known.
The service configuration is valid, yet the air-gapped node lacks all model artifacts and cannot contact the upstream registry.

train: The load generator uses tokenizer files from another Qwen variant, so measured token IDs and server usage disagree for identical text.
Only tokenizer assets were upgraded in the local snapshot and special chat markers are now encoded differently from the model revision.
Client-side prompt lengths no longer align with server accounting because the benchmark silently fetched a newer tokenizer commit.
Requests fail an alignment check after the client points to a tokenizer from a different model family than the running service.
The server is fully offline, but the client cache contains tokenizer.json from another revision and produces different encodings.
validation: Chat template tokens are treated as ordinary text because tokenizer configuration and model weights came from different revisions.
The same prompt maps to different token sequences on client and server after only one side updated its tokenizer snapshot.

train: A model download stops with no space left on device after the filesystem containing the cache reaches one hundred percent usage.
Checkpoint saving fails because the WSL virtual disk has only a few megabytes available, while GPU memory remains below its limit.
Temporary weight shards fill the home partition and the snapshot cannot atomically rename its final file into the cache.
Training writes checkpoints successfully to a larger mount but fails when output_dir is moved back to the nearly full root filesystem.
The cache directory cannot create another safetensors shard due to exhausted disk blocks; network and CUDA are healthy.
validation: Adapter serialization raises an operating-system no-space error and df reports the output volume at full capacity.
The download has enough network bandwidth but cannot write the final artifact because the configured model-cache partition is full.

train: A burst admits far more simultaneous requests than the service capacity and queue delay rises sharply although each request is valid.
Latency SLO failures appear only when arrival rate exceeds sustainable throughput; limiting in-flight work restores stable tails.
The endpoint remains alive but an unbounded client burst creates a growing queue and most requests miss TTFT targets.
Traffic at concurrency four is healthy while concurrency sixty-four overwhelms scheduling and causes timeouts without a model error.
Raw request rate exceeds completion rate for several minutes, so backlog and tail latency continue increasing until clients stop.
validation: The service recovers immediately when new requests are throttled; GPU kernels, artifacts, and dependency versions are otherwise healthy.
A sudden fan-out sends hundreds of valid prompts to one replica and saturates its queue despite adequate capacity under normal load.

train: The configured local model directory is misspelled and does not contain config.json at the resolved path.
Serving points to a parent cache directory rather than the concrete snapshot folder that holds tokenizer and weight files.
The supplied model path exists but references an incomplete transfer with no safetensors shards or manifest.
A relative path resolves from the wrong working directory, so vLLM interprets it as a nonexistent local model location.
Startup rejects the snapshot folder because required tokenizer files were omitted during manual copying.
validation: The command names a directory that was renamed yesterday and validation cannot find any model configuration beneath it.
A local-only launch fails because the selected snapshot path contains metadata but none of the expected weight shard files.

train: The engine selects a precision kernel that is not implemented for the detected GPU compute capability and aborts during initialization.
A quantized dtype requested in the server profile is unsupported by the installed kernels for this graphics architecture.
Model loading reaches kernel selection, then rejects the configured low-precision format despite valid weights and sufficient memory.
The operator reports that the requested floating-point mode requires hardware features absent from the current accelerator.
Switching back to a supported BF16 profile starts correctly, while the experimental precision profile fails capability checks.
validation: The runtime cannot dispatch the requested quantization kernel on this compute architecture and recommends a supported dtype.
An attention backend rejects the configured precision before serving begins because its device capability check does not pass.
